Question_text: Enzymes are used in the fruit juice industry to help with the extraction of juice from fruit. You are going to investigate the extraction of juice from some crushed apple.
Complete the table headings by inserting the units.
Record in the table the volume of juice in measuring cylinders A and B every 2 minutes for 10 minutes.
Use your results to suggest why the use of this enzyme is an advantage in the fruit juice industry.
Suggest reasons for: (i) stirring the contents of beakers A and B (ii) using a clean stirring rod to stir the contents of beaker B.
Explain how the contents of beaker B act as a control.

Some other students did a similar experiment to extract some juice from pears. Their results were: Start Ocm³ After 2 minutes, 12.0 cm³ After 4 minutes, 18.5cm³ After 6 minutes, 21.0 cm³ After 8 minutes, 21.5cm³ After 10 minutes, 22.0 cm³ Use the students' results to construct a line graph. Join your points with ruled, straight lines.
Use your graph to estimate the volume of juice collected at five minutes. Show your working on your graph.
Design an experiment, based on the method you have used, to investigate the effect of the enzyme on the production of juice from different varieties (types) of apple. Give full experimental details.

A student tested some apple juice for the presence of reducing sugar and observed a red colour. Name the testing solution the student used, state a temperature at which the test was carried out and a conclusion for the student's observation.
The photomicrograph shows some human blood cells.
In the space below make a large drawing of the cell labelled C as it appears in the photomicrograph.
Complete the table by describing three visible differences between cell C and cell D.

(i) Draw a straight line on the photomicrograph to join E and F. Measure and record the length of this line. (ii) On your drawing, draw a straight line at the same location as the line E-F. Measure and record the length of this line. (iii) Use your measurements in (i) and (ii) to calculate the magnification of your drawing compared to the photomicrograph.
